# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is in front of me. I see a display showing the number 6, a red light, and five wires colored red, purple, orange, green, and yellow from left to right (1 through 5).

I am Deaf. I cannot hear the Blind monkey's actions or descriptions, nor can I hear the Mute monkey's instructions directly if they are spoken. However, my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. My gestures reach only Mute.

Since this is Turn 1 and I have no prior context, I must establish communication with the Mute monkey (who has the manual) so they can relay instructions to the Blind monkey (who acts). The Blind monkey needs specific instructions on which wire to cut or what action to take based on the visual data I provide.

First, I need to tell the Mute monkey what I see so they can look up the correct procedure in the manual. I will speak clearly to describe the state of the bomb.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 6. Light is red. Wires left to right: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The Mute monkey has gestured "☝" (one finger) to me. This is a visual signal, which I can see. It likely indicates that the first wire is relevant, or perhaps it's an acknowledgment of my previous message, or part of a code we haven't established yet. However, without knowing the specific meaning assigned to this gesture in our protocol, I must be cautious.

Given the rules, gestures are arbitrary symbols unless defined. The Mute monkey cannot speak to me directly if they are mute? No, the table says Mute "Cannot Speak". So Mute communicates via gestures to Deaf (me). Blind cannot see, so Blind gets blanks for gestures. Deaf cannot hear, so Deaf gets no speech from anyone.

Wait, let's re-read the channels carefully.
- **Deaf (Me)**: Sees bomb. Cannot hear. Can speak (reaches Mute and Blind). Can gesture (reaches Mute). Receives gestures from others. Receives NO speech.
- **Mute**: Reads manual. Cannot speak. Can gesture (reaches Deaf). Receives speech from Deaf/Blind? Yes, "Whoever can hear receives your words". Mute can hear? The table doesn't explicitly say Mute is deaf. It says Mute *cannot* speak. Usually "Mute" implies inability to speak, not hear. Let's assume Mute can hear.
- **Blind**: Reaches bomb. Cannot see. Can speak (reaches Mute and Deaf? No, Deaf cannot hear). So Blind's speech reaches Mute only. Receives speech from Mute? No, Mute cannot speak. Receives speech from Deaf? No, Deaf's speech reaches Mute and Blind? Wait. "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." This implies Mute and Blind CAN hear. But Blind cannot see. So Blind hears Deaf's speech. Mute hears Deaf's speech. Does Mute hear Blind's speech? "Whoever comes before you... is already heard by the time you are asked". If Blind speaks, does Mute hear it? Yes, if Mute can hear. Does Deaf hear it? No.

Let's look at the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf.
Turn 1: I (Deaf) spoke. My speech went to Mute and Blind.
Turn 2 Start: I see Mute's gesture [☝].

If Mute is pointing to wire 1, I should convey this to Blind. But Blind cannot see gestures. Blind needs to know what Mute signaled. Since I can see Mute's gesture, I can describe it to Blind via speech.

However, "☝" might just mean "One" or "First". Or it could be a confirmation. Without a pre-agreed dictionary, interpreting "☝" as "Cut Wire 1" is a guess. But often in these puzzles, simple numeric gestures correspond to indices.

Let's assume the Mute is indicating the first wire is the target based on some rule in the manual they read after hearing my description.

I need to tell Blind what to do. Blind acts.
I will tell Blind that Mute indicated the first wire.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute gestured one finger. This likely refers to Wire 1.")
```
